headerBody: India: Tourist Scams documents 60 specific scams against Indian police and consumer-protection sources — state Tourist Police units, the Ministry of Tourism's 1363 helpline, and the National Consumer Helpline (1915) — plus r/IndiaTravel reports and verified Indian news from The Times of India and News18. The exact scripts, the tells that give them away, and the plain Hindi phrases that shut them down. Each one is drawn as an Amar Chitra Katha 1970s-80s comic-book panel so you recognize the setup before the pitch lands. Sourced against the record, not recycled from blog lists.
quadHead: Four ways India catches tourists off guard.

quad.title: The Taj-Area Marble Factory Tour
quad.tl: Your driver routes the day to a Tajganj "marble factory" where a polite owner walks you past artisans tapping pietra dura, serves chai, then pushes inlay bowls at ₹33,000 to USD 2,500 — the same piece runs ₹2,500 to ₹4,000 at Sadar Bazaar, and the driver takes a cut of whatever you buy. Refuse every driver-suggested shop and price marble at three bazaar vendors first.

quad.title: The Johari Bazaar Gem-Export Pitch
quad.tl: A charming "gem trader" buys you chai near Johari Bazaar and offers an investment: carry ₹45,000 of Jaipur rubies and sapphires through customs and split the resale profit — the stones turn out to be colored glass and no buyer is ever waiting. Never buy gems as investment items from an unsolicited stranger, and walk the moment anyone wants to use you as a courier.

quad.title: The CST Black-Taxi Meter Scam
quad.tl: A black-and-yellow kaali peeli at CST, the Gateway of India or the airport keeps the meter off, produces a laminated "rate card," and a 20-minute Bandra-to-Colaba ride that should run ₹180 is billed at ₹800. Insist on the meter before you get in, or book the ride in an app with a fixed fare.

quad.title: The Motorbike-Rental Damage Claim
quad.tl: A North Goa scooter shop pockets your ₹2,000 to ₹5,000 deposit by "discovering" a scratch on return that you photographed clear before riding off — sometimes scratching the bike themselves while you are away. Film a slow walk-around of the whole bike with the owner on camera before you take the keys.

body: India: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented against Indian police and consumer-protection sources — state Tourist Police units, the Ministry of Tourism's 1363 helpline, and the National Consumer Helpline (1915) — plus r/IndiaTravel and r/india_tourism reports and verified Indian news from The Times of India and News18. Sourced and re-reported, not recycled from blog lists.

60 specific scams across Delhi, Agra, Jaipur, Mumbai, Varanasi, Udaipur, Goa and five more destinations — the fake railway-station tourist office, the Tajganj marble-factory tour, the Johari Bazaar gem-export pitch, the kaali peeli meter switch, the Ganga Aarti offering shake-down, the scooter-deposit shakedown. The exact scripts, the red flags that give them away, and the Hindi phrases that shut them down, romanized so you can read them aloud and shown in Devanagari you can hold up on your phone.
Scams evolve, so the book is re-researched every year, and the current edition sits in your Kindle library. Built for the traveler who wants to move through India relaxed, not braced.
